question: Who among the following was appointed as Executive Director of the Reserve Bank of India in March 2025 to look after Department of Statistics and Information Management and Financial Stability Department?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. Ajit Ratnakar Joshi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. Ajit Ratnakar Joshi** was appointed as the **Executive Director** of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** in **March 2025**.
 
• He is responsible for overseeing two critical departments of the RBI:
 
 
• The **Department of Statistics and Information Management (DSIM)**, which handles statistical analysis, data collection, and information management to support RBI's policy decisions.
 
• The **Financial Stability Department (FSD)**, which ensures the stability of India's financial system by identifying and mitigating systemic risks.
 
 
 
• **Dr. Ajit Ratnakar Joshi** is known for his extensive experience in economics, finance, and data analysis, making him well-suited for these vital roles in RBI.
 
• His appointment aligns with RBI's objective of strengthening its analytical and data-driven approach to policy formulation and maintaining financial stability in India.
 
• He has previously held important positions in various financial institutions and is recognized for his contributions to economic policymaking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**

 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is the central banking institution of India, responsible for regulating the country's monetary policy and ensuring financial stability.
 
• It was established on **1 April 1935**, under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• The RBI performs functions such as issuing currency, managing foreign exchange reserves, regulating and supervising banks, and acting as the banker to the government.
 
 
 
• **Department of Statistics and Information Management (DSIM):**
 
 
• This department collects, compiles, and analyzes macroeconomic and financial statistics critical for policymaking.
 
• It also develops statistical methodologies and manages the digital infrastructure for data storage and dissemination.
 
• The DSIM is instrumental in conducting surveys, such as the Consumer Confidence Survey and Inflation Expectations Survey, which aid the RBI in decision-making.
 
 
 
• **Financial Stability Department (FSD):**
 
 
• Established in 2010, the FSD is tasked with monitoring the stability of India's financial system.
 
• It identifies systemic risks, conducts stress testing, and formulates measures to prevent financial crises.
 
• The department also publishes the **Financial Stability Report**, which provides a comprehensive assessment of the health of the financial sector.
 
 
 
• **Executive Directors in RBI:**
 
 
• Executive Directors (EDs) play a pivotal role in implementing RBI's policies and managing its various departments.
 
• They typically have extensive experience in banking, finance, economics, or related fields and are responsible for key operational areas of the central bank.
 
• The appointment of EDs is crucial for ensuring effective governance and operational efficiency within the RBI.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **RBI** is headquartered in **Mumbai** and has multiple regional offices across India.
 
• The **Governor** of RBI is the chief executive officer, supported by Deputy Governors and Executive Directors.
 
• In recent years, the RBI has emphasized the importance of data-driven decision-making to enhance policy effectiveness and transparency.
 
• The **Financial Stability Report (FSR)**, published semi-annually by the FSD, provides key insights into the health of the banking and financial sectors.
 
• The DSIM has been at the forefront of modernizing statistical practices and adopting advanced data analytics to support the RBI's regulatory and supervisory functions.
